## PDF page 52

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=52)

```text
                                  CHAPTER FOUR



                                  COMBOS


Combos, combinations, combinatorics. They all mean the same thing. They
mean we are looking at ranges from a mathematical perspective and
counting the ways our opponent can make certain hands.

Essentially, we are working out how many different ways a specific hand can
exist in a given situation.

If you ask a new player how many combos there are of Ace King, they are
likely to say “one.” Afterall, AK is just a single hand. But that is not how tech-
nical players look at the game. The fact is that there are 16 total combos of
Ace King, which includes 4 suited combos and 12 unsuited combos.


  suited                      A               A           A               A
                                  K                K          K               K

                         A            A           A       A       A           A
                              K           K           K       K       K           K
                         A            A           A       A       A           A
                              K           K           K       K       K           K
   off suit
                                      PA G E 5 2
```

## PDF page 53

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=53)

```text
                              COMBOS: SIMPLIFIED


Instead of boring you with a stats lesson on combinations and permutations,
I will just give you this very simple table to memorize for common preflop
hand types.

            HAND TYPE                      COMBOS                 EXAMPLE
            Pocket Pair                           6                   AA
          Unpaired Hand                          16                   KQ
         Unpaired & Suited                       4                    98s
        Unpaired & Unsuited                      12                   42o

Just remember that there are 6 combos of every pocket pair and 16 of every
unpaired hand. The 16 includes both the 12 unsuited and 4 suited versions.
Not too scary, right?

The good news is that the more you practice this, the more internalized and
automated this becomes. Eventually, you will be able to quickly visualize
ranges as a collection of specific hands, %-form, and combos all at the same
time. So stay focused while going through these examples, even if they seem
a little boring at first.

And finally, given that this workbook is focused on preflop play, this section
is geared toward the combos of preflop hands and ranges. We will do an
intense exploration of postflop combos in an upcoming workbook.

TOOLS TO USE: Flopzilla, Equilab, or PokerCruncher will work. Seasoned players
should be able to do this first section off the top of their heads.

PROCESS: Quickly jot down the number of combos for each starting hand.

TAKEAWAYS: Notice the difference in combos for suited vs. unsuited versions
of hands. Also, notice how many more unpaired hand combos exist com-
pared to pocket pair combos.

GLGL.

                                    PA G E 5 3
```
